Samir Patel: Heads-up — after the kernel-selector change on canary I'm seeing bursts of small OOM spikes (mostly logits/scratchpad). repro attached in thread.
runtime-bot: deploy 2026-03-17T09:12:03Z to canary finished (id: d2f7).
Jess Li: Ugh, saw one earlier too. Any pattern on sequence length or batch size?
Samir Patel: Mostly seqs around 1024-2048 and batches of 4-12. KV cache looks fine, this is happening during decode after a kernel fallback to split-softmax.
Mika Torres: Interesting — split-softmax increases temporary logits workspace by ~1.8x for N_VOCAB-aligned buffers. Could be alignment/round-up policy in tensor pool.
Anya K.: Can you paste the profiler slice showing allocation spikes? small snippet helps.
Samir Patel: Pasted — flame: alloc->free churn aligns with 'logits_scratch' allocations right after kernel switch.
Samir Patel: ```
# short repro command
./serving_canary --model gpt-13b --seq 1536 --batch 8 --trace alloc,kv,ker
# profiler excerpt (condensed)
[12:02:13.345] allocate logits_scratch 34.2MB
[12:02:13.346] allocate kv_prefetch 12.8MB
[12:02:13.349] free logits_scratch 34.2MB
[12:02:13.350] allocate logits_scratch 61.6MB  <-- sudden jump after kernel fallback
```
Jess Li: That sudden jump screams rounding policy difference. If our pool slabs are sized for 'typical' fused-softmax sizes, split-softmax will request larger contiguous buffer and force a new allocation. Frequent allocate/free for those sizes leads to fragmentation.
Mika Torres: Two quick mitigations: 1) per-kernel buffer size hints so pool can hold a slot for the split-softmax shape; 2) change pool rounding to power-of-two up to 64KB then to page multiples for larger to avoid cross-slab allocations.
Anya K.: Also check KV cache reuse windows — if we free scratchpads too eagerly while KV still pinned in a different stream, we can get transient spikes. Any cross-stream frees?
Samir Patel: Good call. Trace shows scratchpad frees happening on completion callback in different CUDA stream than the allocate. Might be delayed reclaim + allocator compaction race.
Jess Li: Could be exacerbated by batching heuristics: when batch sizes vary fast, we oscillate between allocations of two different approx sizes. We should track per-route batch-size histogram and guide pool sizing.
Mika Torres: Quick experiment I ran locally: changed pool_rounding from 4KB to 256KB for logits_scratch. Repro 1k decode requests -> before: 7 OOMs in 1k, after: 0 OOMs, 95th latency +2.1%. Memory steady.
Samir Patel: Nice. Can you share the minimal patch?
Mika Torres: ```diff
- pool_rounding: 4096
+ pool_rounding: 262144  # logits scratch: coarse rounding to reduce fragmentation
```
Anya K.: That's a blunt instrument but pragmatic. We should instead implement per-buffer-class rounding and eviction priority: keep a few large logits slots pinned for split-softmax. Also add metric: pool_miss_rate_by_size_bucket.
Jess Li: Agree. Actionable plan: (1) Samir open issue + repro; (2) Mika prepare PR with per-class rounding and keep-count; (3) Jess add telemetry for miss rate and batch-size histogram; (4) Anya validate KV stream-safe frees.
Samir Patel: I'll open the issue with the repro trace & flame and attach the canary logs. Will mark P0 for the canary since it causes intermittent OOMs.
Mika Torres: I'll schedule a 2h canary run after PR. Quick note: also add small optimization to prefer reusing slightly-smaller slab if within 8% to reduce churn.
Jess Li: I'll add dashboards and an alert when pool_miss_rate_by_size_bucket > 5% for >10m.
Samir Patel: Thanks all. If PR lands today, I'll run extended canary overnight and post results. :thumbsup:
